as_written_in_papers.quote: The panel detected the presence of two novel compound heterozygous mutations in the LPIN2 gene: I716Vfs*2 (c.2144_2145dupGT) and p. E565Kfs*15 (c.1693_1694delGA) frameshifts.

cases.statement: One affected girl of Italian (central-European) ancestry from non-consanguineous parents, compound heterozygous with c.1693_1694del (PMID 39255247).

people.label: patient (single case)
people.key_phenotypes: onset at 6 months with elbow swelling and low-grade fever; multifocal STIR hyperintensity of long bones with periosteal reaction; microcytic anaemia with dyserythropoiesis on bone marrow; splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy; no skin involvement

quotes.quote: The girl, first child of non-consanguineous Caucasian Italian parents, at the age of 6 months presented swelling of the right elbow associated with low-grade fever.

The blood tests confirmed microcytic anaemia (Hb 10 g/dl, mean corpuscolar volume (MCV) 65 fl) with leucocytes and platelets within the normal range, increased inflammatory markers (CRP 8.59 mg/dl, ESR 43 mm/1 h, serum amyloid A 702 mg/l) and hypergammaglobulinemia.
MRI revealed STIR hyper-intensity and contrast enhancement of the spongy osseous tissue of femur distal diaphysis and distal metaphysis, tibia proximal epiphysis and part of the diaphysis.
A bone marrow aspirate showed increased trilinear cellularity with ineffective erythropoiesis and signs of dyserythropoiesis: binuclear/trinuclear erythroblasts and inter-nuclear bridging (Fig. 1D).
Multiple lymphadenopathies and splenomegaly were also detected.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Early-onset multifocal sterile osteomyelitis (bone biopsy, negative microbiology) with dyserythropoietic microcytic anaemia, which matches the syndrome as the authors describe it; no skin lesions. She had a large NGS panel for autoinflammatory and immunodeficiency genes; the paper does not state results for other genes. Neutropenia appeared during anti-IL-1 treatment.

quotes.quote: A bone biopsy of the proximal right tibial metaphysis showed irregular thickening of the trabeculae, with numerous active osteoblasts and osteoclasts at the surface.
Microbiological investigations were negative.
In light of the clinical picture, a large next-generation sequencing (NGS) diagnostic panel for autoinflammatory diseases and immunodeficiencies was performed.

Our case, in which no skin involvement was observed, confirms that Majeed syndrome should be suspected not only in the presence of the ‘triad’ typical of the disease but rather in presence of a systemic inflammatory disease, with prevalent bone involvement, especially in case of presence of signs of dyserythropoietic anaemia.

segregation.statement: No other affected relatives reported. Mother carries this variant; father carries the other. Parents' clinical status is not described; the proband is the first child.

quotes.quote: The first mutation, at exon 16, was inherited from the mother, while the second, at exon 12, was inherited from the father.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo: inherited from the mother. Both parents were tested. Parentage confirmation is not reported.

quotes.quote: The first mutation, at exon 16, was inherited from the mother, while the second, at exon 12, was inherited from the father.

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.1693_1694delGA (p.E565Kfs*15) from the father. Phase was shown by parental testing; confirmed by Sanger.

quotes.quote: The first mutation, at exon 16, was inherited from the mother, while the second, at exon 12, was inherited from the father.
The mutations were confirmed by Sanger analysis.
The NGS panel performed revealed two novel frameshift mutations in both alleles, inherited from parents and therefore compatible with compound heterozygosity

functional.statement: Assay on the patient's own cells (freshly isolated peripheral blood monocytes), not a construct, and not specific to this variant (it reflects the compound heterozygous genotype). LPS-stimulated monocytes secreted IL-1β faster than cells from healthy donors (n = 3), and IL-1α, TNF-α and IL-1RA were also raised. Secretion dropped after 3 months of anakinra. The authors say the test confirmed pathogenicity.

quotes.quote: As shown in Fig. 2A, the kinetics of the IL-1β secretion is much faster in the patient (black square) than in healthy monocytes [health donors (HD)] (white circle).
Similarly, secretion of IL-1α, TNF-α and IL-1RA was increased in LPS-stimulated patient monocytes collected before treatment.
After 3 months of treatment with anakinra, patient monocytes secreted less IL-1β (Fig. 2A).

Kinetics of IL-1β (A), IL-1α (B), TNF-α (C) and IL-1RA (D) after LPS stimulation (200 ng/ml) from peripheral blood monocytes isolated from the patient before and after therapy and from healthy donors (HD) (n = 3).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: A 2-bp duplication causing a frameshift, p.(Ile716ValfsTer2) (from the batch HGVS; it agrees with the paper). The authors expect truncation or nonsense-mediated decay and describe the disease as loss of function.

quotes.quote: Respectively, c.2144_2145dupGT leads to a premature stop codon at position 2 amino acids after the mutation, while c.1693_1694delGA creates a new reading frame that ends with a stop at position 15 after the mutation.
Both variants are expected to produce a truncated protein or, more likely, to lead to early degradation of mRNA through the mechanism of nonsense-mediated decay.
Majeed syndrome is an autosomal recessive monogenic autoinflammatory disease caused by loss-of-function mutations in the LPIN2 gene.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Absent from INFEVERS, gnomAD, 1000 Genomes and dbSNP per the authors.

quotes.quote: The mutations detected in our patient are not reported in the INFEVERS database [16] or in other human sequence databases (gnomAD, 1000 Genomes Project, dbSNP).
Both variants were classified as pathogenic variants (PVS1-PM2-PP4) according to the ACMG guidelines [17].

concerns: The functional assay (monocyte cytokine secretion) uses the patient's cells with both variants; it is not specific to this variant.
The paper writes the protein change without 'p.' (I716Vfs*2) and the cDNA as c.2144_2145dupGT. No transcript is named; exon 16 is the authors' numbering.
The parents' phenotypes and zygosity are not described in words; only 'inherited from the mother/father'.
Neutropenia during treatment: the authors considered an anakinra side effect and also cite neutropenia as a possible disease feature.
Same person also carries candidate G-majeed-011 (c.1693_1694del).
notes_for_panel: A single compound heterozygous case with phase set by parental testing and Sanger confirmation. The authors state ACMG criteria. The patient-cell cytokine data are genotype-level, not variant-level.
